entries.title: Proverbs 29:4
segments:
CHAP. XXIX. 
 
  V. 4. Judgment-By the free and impartial exercise of justice. Gifts-Bribes.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:8
segments: V. 8. Wrath-The wrath of God or of men, who were enraged against it.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:9
segments: V. 9. Whether-Whether he, the wise man, deal sharply with him, or mildly, there is no rest, no end or fruit of the debate.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:15
segments: V. 15. Left-Suffered to follow his own will without restraint and chastening.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:18
segments: V. 18. No vision-No prophecy; no publick preaching of God's word.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:19
segments: V. 19. A servant-Who is so not only in condition, but also in the temper of his mind, disingenuous, and stubborn.  Words-By mere words. Tho'-Though he know thy mind, and his own duty.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:20
segments: V. 20. Hasty-Who is rash and heady in the management of his affairs.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:21
segments: V. 21. Delicately-Allowing him too much freedom, and familiarity. A son-Will find him at last grow insolent, and forgetful of his servile condition.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:24
segments: V. 24. Bewrayeth it not-Which he is bound to do for the publick good.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:25
segments: V. 25. A snare-Is an occasion of many sins.

entries.title: Proverbs 29:26
segments: V. 26. Judgment-The decision of his cause, and the success of all his endeavours.
